calls.head: Shots should fly both ways
calls.body: Nashville’s games average 84.5 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (4th of 32 for pace); Toronto’s average 84.4 (5th).
calls.call: The game runs at more than the two teams’ usual 84.4 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 81.8 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 84.5 and a league average of 82.0.

calls.head: Nashville kills penalties far better than Toronto
calls.body: Nashville ranks 16th of 32 for penalty kill, toward the airtight end; Toronto ranks 31st, toward the leaky end.
calls.call: Nashville’s penalty kill allows less per 60 than Toronto’s.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On expected goals allowed per 60 on the penalty kill, Nashville had 12.3 per 60 and Toronto 34.3 per 60. Coming in, Nashville was at 7.5 per 60 and Toronto at 8.4 per 60.

TOR.head: We had this close to even (44% for Toronto), and Toronto came through.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (56% for Nashville), and it went Toronto’s way.

surprises.head: Nashville got to the dangerous areas
surprises.body: Nashville needed 10.9 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 17.0 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 60 games.

surprises.head: Nashville shortened its bench
surprises.body: Nashville’s bottom-six forwards played 38% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against its usual 42% and a league average of 42%. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 9 games.
